# dsh-model-rotator
> 简体中文 | **English** | Changelog
Model auto-ranking and transparent failover for DeepSeek Harness.

When the current model hits a quota wall, an expired credential, a rate limit or
a transient network

error, this plugin switches to the next-best configured
model **inside the same turn** — and the us
er sees an ordinary reply.
## What it does

1. **Discovers** every dialable `provider/model` on this machine
(`ctx.llm.listProviders()` + each a

dapter's `listModels()`).
2. **Filters** out families that cannot answer a chat turn — embeddings,
r

erankers, ASR/TTS, OCR, image/video generation, content moderators and
judges. Dialing one of those

can only fail the turn and burn a cooldown slot
that a real model could have used.
3. **Skips the im

age-reading mode.** dsh-vision-router wraps a chat route into a
twin (`<provider>-vision`) whose onl

y job is to add image reading to that same
model. It is one model reachable twice, not a second one,

so failing a text
turn over into it would answer through the image pipeline — and the
same-model pr

eference below would rank the twin *first*. Those routes are
therefore never candidates (a model id

that merely *mentions* vision is still
a chat model and stays). The model list can switch one back o

n when a wrapper
name does not follow the convention.
4. **Ranks** the survivors by measured connect

ivity (Laplace-smoothed success
rate), speed (median TTFT and throughput) and an active failure cool

down. A
model that *is* the current one — or a close relative of it — on another
provider carries a

bonus, because the model you picked is usually the model
you want, just from a working channel.
4. *

*Retries before it believes a failure.** A provider fails transiently: a
rate-limit blip, a reset so

cket, an overloaded channel. One miss therefore
does not count as a fault — the same model gets `ret

riesPerModel` more tries
(2 by default, 0–5), `retryBackoffMs` apart (300 ms, then the double of it)

,
before the failure is acted on. A retry is not a switch: it asks nothing and
changes nothing.
5. *

*Fails over** at the `llm/stream` waterfall: attempt 1 is the untouched
harness path; a failure that

produced **no content at all** abandons that
attempt, closes its upstream stream, and re-dispatches

the next candidate as
a fresh `ctx.llm.stream()` — the same model first while retries remain, then

e as
a fresh `ctx.llm.stream()` — the same model first while retries remain, then
the ranking above.

Once any content chunk has been yielded the attempt is never retried — a second
[该节后续省略]
### What counts as content

"Flow" is the switch that closes the retry window, so it means *the user has been
shown reply text*

— and nothing weaker. A `reasoning-delta` is not content: the
harness folds reasoning away again whe

n a retry happens, which is exactly what
makes retrying a reasoning-loop or reasoning-effort failure

safe. Markup chunks
(`block-start`, or a `block-end` carrying a reasoning block) are not content
ei

ther. Counting those was a real defect: a live model looked dead because a
block-start closed the wi
ndow and the very next error was taken as final.
### Automatic calls are not conversation turns

A compaction summary and a session title ride the same `llm/stream` seam but are
not a user turn. Th

eir refusals are usually statements about *that lane* — a
proxy answering "bili owns compression her

e" — so asking a second provider to
carry the plumbing is the wrong reflex: it burns a real model on

work nobody
reads, and it is the single loudest source of spurious switching. The plugin
therefore

passes any call carrying `purpose: "compaction"` or
`purpose: "session-title"` straight through, err

or included. An unnamed call —
every ordinary turn — keeps failing over exactly as before.
## Announcing a switch

A switch is otherwise silent: the reply simply arrives from a different model.
The plugin now record

s it on the **Model switches** tab, beside 对话 / 轨迹 /
上下文, one row per switch — when it happened, whi

ch model answered instead, and
why:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The tab reads the plugin's own record
(`GET /_dsh/model-rotator/switches?session=<id>`), so a switch

costs **no
conversation context**. The conversation it belongs to is **injected by the Host**
— the

cell registers `inject: (sessionId) => ({ sessionId })` and reads
`props.sessionId`, the same contr

act the built-in 对话 and 轨迹 tabs use (before
0.2.11 it read a field the Host never had, so the tab co

uld not tell which
conversation it was in). Records are filed per conversation, and the session is
b

ound **where the switch happens** — `ctx.get('agents').currentInitiator()` answers
with the agent th

at started the call — rather than at the turn boundary, which is
process-wide: whichever conversatio

n stops a turn next would otherwise drain the
queue and take everyone else's rows with it. A call wi

th no live turn (a plugin
route, a host without `agents`) still records, with an empty session; empt

y-session
rows appear only in the every-session view.

When this conversation has no rows of its own but the log is not empty, the tab
falls back to **ever

y conversation's** rows and labels the view as such, so history
never reads as "nothing happened".

If you also want the old line in the transcript, turn `noticeSwitch` on and the
plugin posts it as b

efore — `模型已切换：A → B`, with the failure kind in brackets
when it is known (`(quota)`, `(rate-limit)`

ore — `模型已切换：A → B`, with the failure kind in brackets
when it is known (`(quota)`, `(rate-limit)`).
| Behaviour | |

## What it does NOT do

It never reads, writes or rewrites model/provider configuration. It does not
touch `cordis.patch.yml

`, `agent-default-model`, `llm-pi-ai` or any provider
registration. It only observes the stream wate

-model`, `llm-pi-ai` or any provider
registration. It only observes the stream waterfall at runtime.
